claims.text: The starting alloy is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a single-phase random solid solution with minimal inherent short-range order.
Thermo-mechanical aging can increase short-range order while avoiding secondary-phase formation in CoCrFeNiTi.
Thermo-mechanical aging promotes atomic rearrangements that increase local ordering in the matrix.
Localized short-range-ordered domains act as obstacles to dislocation glide.
Increased short-range order raises hardness by impeding dislocation motion.
Increased short-range order raises yield strength by impeding dislocation motion.
Enhanced dislocation pinning may reduce ductility relative to the as-cast state.
Aged CoCrFeNiTi containing more short-range order will have higher hardness than the as-cast alloy.
Aged CoCrFeNiTi containing more short-range order will have higher yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
Aged CoCrFeNiTi will show a modest reduction in plasticity relative to the as-cast alloy.
The proposed SRO-related mechanical-property effects will occur under quasi-static loading at both 25 °C and 600 °C.
As-cast nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength.
As-cast nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability.
The favorable plasticity and machinability of the as-cast alloy are due to the absence of significant short-range order.
The hypothesis is limited to single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi without secondary-phase precipitation.
The hypothesis applies from 25 °C to 600 °C under quasi-static loading and before extensive plastic deformation.
The cited Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni study reports high-temperature short-range ordering and chemical clustering.
The cited Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni study reports that high-strain compression promotes atomistic rearrangements in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.

contradictions.description: The boundary limits the hypothesis to conditions before extensive plastic deformation, whereas the proposed ductility and plastic-strain measurements necessarily require deformation into the plastic regime and may extend to large strain.
